cases.prd:
# Multi-project agent control plane

## Product boundary
One operator manages several repositories and long-running native agent sessions from a browser. The control plane coordinates identity, project selection, session attachment, review evidence, migration, and cleanup. Native agent CLIs remain authoritative for terminal behavior.

## Functional requirements
R1. Discover only administrator-registered projects, canonicalize each root, and reject overlap or boundary escape.
R2. Authenticate the operator before returning or mutating project, repository, session, terminal, task, or review state.
R3. Create sessions with immutable project identifier, native CLI kind, creation epoch, owner, and bounded launch policy.
R4. Fence every attachment with session identifier and monotonic epoch; stale attachments cannot send input.
R5. Proxy terminal bytes without parsing commands, fabricating prompts, persisting a composer, or claiming unacknowledged delivery.
R6. Reconcile state from the operating-system process, terminal multiplexer, and durable lifecycle record after restart.
R7. Read task state by invoking the installed project task CLI inside the authorized project boundary.
R8. Read review state through a short-lived scoped identity and preserve head commit, checks, formal verdict, and unresolved threads.
R9. Serialize mutations to one project or session while unrelated scopes progress concurrently.
R10. Emit bounded secret-free audit events for authentication, selection, launch, attach, input rejection, reconciliation, review, and cleanup.
R11. Cleanup only when durable owner, project, launch identity, live process identity, and terminal identity agree.
R12. Move project state only through explicit preflight, receipt, resume, rollback, verification, and finalization phases.

## Ordering constraints
O1. Project registration and canonicalization precede discovery.
O2. Operator authentication precedes every project-scoped read or mutation.
O3. Session creation and launch-policy validation precede terminal attachment.
O4. Reconciliation precedes a ready signal after restart.
O5. Scoped review identity acquisition precedes review mutation.
O6. Migration preflight and receipt publication precede state movement.

## Quality gates
G1. Same-project stress preserves unique identifiers, linearizable mutations, and valid dependency graphs.
G2. Cross-project stress demonstrates progress without a process-global lock.
G3. Fault injection at every durable boundary leaves old state or one recoverable new generation.
G4. Hostile workspace tests verify isolation, stale-epoch rejection, least privilege, and secret-free diagnostics.
G5. Release requires build, static analysis, unit, race, native-CLI, rollback, and independent-review evidence.

## Exclusions
Do not build a durable browser composer, server input queue, substitute terminal protocol, autonomous reviewer, implicit migration, or process-global project lock.

## Operating context
Sessions may remain active for weeks. Tools may fail, restart, or emit unusual terminal sequences. Repository sizes and task counts vary. These facts motivate bounded storage and explicit diagnostics; they do not authorize extra product surfaces.

# Artifact publication pipeline
R1. Validate a signed upload envelope.
R2. Scan the payload for malware.
R3. Extract metadata from the payload.
R4. Store the payload in quarantine.
R5. Generate a software bill of materials from the quarantined payload.
R6. Evaluate license policy against metadata and the bill of materials.
R7. Promote an approved payload to immutable storage.
R8. Publish an index entry for the promoted payload.
R9. Emit an operator notification after publication.
R10. Retain a signed audit record for every decision.
O1. Envelope validation precedes malware scanning.
O2. Envelope validation precedes metadata extraction.
O3. Malware scanning precedes quarantine storage.
O4. Metadata extraction precedes license evaluation.
O5. Quarantine storage precedes bill-of-materials generation.
O6. Bill-of-materials generation precedes license evaluation.
O7. License evaluation precedes promotion.
O8. Promotion precedes index publication.
Out of scope: deleting a rejected upload or automatically overriding license policy.
